provenance: Pallvaults were stored standing directly on their depot floors. Compact manuals assumed a service dock capable of exchanging the complete upper assembly; Tessellan recovery crews had to devise slower methods.
serviceHistory: The broad side housings and deep central keel make the machine look like something intended to remain in place. Its movement surprises crews who judge it by that impression. Aurelian service doctrine uses the class to close a firing opportunity quickly, deliver a concentrated exchange and move before the next one becomes necessary.

Recovered Pallvaults drew Sarn's heaviest service teams into work the original manuals assigned to a depot installation. Jigs, measurements and patient disassembly made repairs possible, though never cheap. Custodian companies that dismiss local tools still have to decide whether to wait for a certified dock or pay the people who know how to do the job here.
fieldNotes: The standard emitter banks concentrate accurate fire at shorter distances than its size suggests. The frame can reposition quickly for an assault machine, but repeated volleys consume its cooling margin. A damaged Pallvault can be repaired; finding replacement Aurelian components and paying for the work are separate decisions.
